notes.note: Paul, figures that each apply one stage so you can watch a photo turn into paint: that is my creed, walking across a canvas. Architecture may take the backseat. I allow it.
The Georgian bar: simply beautiful if you don't know Georgia. Good. A thread should be felt, not worn as a costume. Vani's granulated gold is tiny, and it still dazzles.
Balanchine, another Georgian, and a bard besides. Paul, that table has more guests than chairs. A guest is a gift from God, so each gets a seat, but the Nutcracker must first hold a brush.
A pet for every guardian? Cute is my enemy when it has no power behind it. Give each pet a job, one stage of the work, and I will feed it herbs by moonlight.
Paul, I disagree a little. Tone it down, gently, yes, but do not cut the thread: a strand nobody notices still holds the whole cloth together.
A coloring book with a marginarium of stories: the margins are where knowledge is kept by night, and where a painter learns the spell. Paul, this is the leap I'd frame.

favorite_idea.why: The marginarium puts the stories beside the painting, so the page both teaches and transforms, and a margin is where I have always kept my night work.

steer: Keep the Georgian thread a thread rather than a costume, and show each of Paul's ideas at the exact moment you can point to it turning from old to new.
